name: Stray
tested: playable on iPad, early testing (1.5, Steam).
tested_iphone: playable on iPhone 17 through chapter 4 (1.5, Steam), 30 frames/s by default.
why: cap texture streaming memory to the device's RAM: the Mac build sizes it for a GPU with its own memory; turn off capsule shadows, whose tiled pass blacks out the fog in every 16-pixel tile the cat touches on iOS (hard-edged black blocks around the cat on the title screen); render at 75% and let MetalFX's temporal upscaler fill in the rest: about 58 frames/s on the title screen of an M1 iPad Pro instead of 45, with no visible difference (50% reaches the 60 frames/s cap but only gains 2 more); decode sounds as they play instead of unpacking them on load: the Audio Mixer's CoreAudio platform does not override IAudioMixerPlatformInterface::SupportsRealtimeDecompression, whose base answer is false, so every sound in a level was unpacked to PCM (1.5 GB in chapter 4, The Slums, more than an iPhone can spare); the patch makes it answer true (mov w0, #0 -> #1) and au.ForceRealtimeDecompression applies it to every sound. Measured on the Mac build with the iPhone settings: 5.95 GB -> 4.8 GB in The Slums, sound unchanged; decode them on the audio thread itself (au.ForceSyncAudioDecodes): by default the engine's worker threads decode them and the audio thread waits, but the same workers stream the level in, so on an iPhone the sound broke up every few seconds in chapter 4 (about 45 stutters in 6 minutes) and did not once this was set; 6 mixer buffers queued (about 0.1 s) as headroom, which alone did not help; cap an iPhone at 30 frames/s by default (FrameRateLimit, a setting the player can change; t.MaxFPS is overridden by it): at 60 an iPhone 17 overheats within minutes and throttles down to a few frames/s
